tasks.short: Educate the public about fire safety and prevention

steps.what: Find current fire safety information relevant to the audience
Prepare the educational material used with the public

loop.purpose: Adapt existing safety information to the current audience
loop.input: Selected current prevention sources and audience description
loop.check: The specialist checks every safety statement against current sources and checks audience suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported advice or unclear meaning returns to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing material should be reused first; a bounded draft helps only where wording needs audience-specific adaptation.

steps.what: Check educational material for accuracy and practical clarity
Educate the public and answer fire prevention questions

tasks.design: Reuse current prevention sources in {DOCS}, with a bounded drafting loop only for material that already needs audience adaptation. The specialist checks all advice and retains public teaching and questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing audience-specific explanations can repeat existing safety information.
tasks.enabler_now: Current source material supports checked adaptation rather than unsupported generated advice.
tasks.still_hard: People need practical explanations responsive to their circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise misunderstanding and adapt the conversation safely.
tasks.altitude: Prepare relevant material while preserving direct public engagement.

reach.learn: Adapt checked sources to the audience.

evidence.claim: The digest identifies Brandweer.nl topic pages as source material for public education; their use for checked drafting is a proposed design, not measured savings.

assumptions: Preparation is included only where material is already used in current public education; no attendance report or trailing log is added.

The specialist identifies audience needs during current preparation and selects source versions in s1, with that capture and checking time retained. Missing or unsuitable advice returns to manual source research.
Native document search removes 2 hours of repeated navigation. Drafting removes 7 hours of source restatement; substantive checking and the public session remain fully retained.
Reuse existing material before generation. Ordinary internal saves remain retained and ungated.
unknowns: How often current material genuinely needs rewriting.
research_questions: Compare complete preparation time including advice checking for several audiences.

already_counted.description: Check advice and teach the public

incremental.description: Maintain source selections and drafting checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact material and advice presented to the current audience; the specialist checks changed statements before delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=91, gross 9 minus 2 upkeep gives central net 7. Conservative case: unsuitable source indexing retains all 10 lookup hours and difficult adaptation retains 18/20 writing hours, plus 70 fixed: 98 retained, 2 gross minus 2 =0. Suitable existing pages retain 9 lookup and 15 adaptation hours plus 70 fixed: 94 retained, 6 gross minus 2 =4.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct firefighting equipment maintenance and requisition replacements

steps.what: Retrieve firefighting equipment history and current specifications
Assess whether the equipment needs maintenance, repair or replacement
Write the maintenance or repair work request
Communicate maintenance and repair directions to colleagues
Oversee maintenance progress and resolve equipment issues
Prepare a new equipment requisition where replacement is needed
Submit the equipment requisition to purchasing colleagues

tasks.design: Configure equipment-linked work requests in {OPS_SYSTEM} and reuse verified equipment identity in {PROCUREMENT} requisitions. Retain condition assessment, maintenance direction and oversight, and the checked requisition handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment identifiers and service history may be repeatedly located and copied into work requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset views and existing request fields can remove specific repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Whether equipment can safely remain in service requires judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a routine repair from a condition requiring replacement or escalation.
tasks.altitude: Direct maintenance with less repeated asset administration.

reach.learn: Keep directions linked to the correct asset and current condition.

evidence.claim: Native asset-linked work requests and requisition fields could reduce repeated entry; the benefit is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Shares describe a current portfolio containing repair and replacement cases, not a requirement to perform both branches on every item. Existing work requests are read by maintenance and requisitions by purchasing; no trailing activity log is added.

Asset staff maintain equipment identifiers and specifications; maintenance staff produce dated service history. S1 includes retrieval and checking. The specialist produces condition findings and the decision in s2, and captures the work request/requisition in retained s3/s6 time. Missing identifiers require manual resolution.

The asset view removes 2 navigation hours. The work-request form removes 8 hours of repeated asset/history headings. Requisition defaults remove only 1 hour of identifiers because the equipment specification remains individual.
Native fields come first. Ordinary saves remain retained without self-approval; actual colleague handoffs have separate gates.
unknowns: Which work-request fields are repeated today.
Whether requisitions already prefill equipment identity.
research_questions: Time current repair and replacement cases separately and validate the portfolio shares.

incremental.description: Maintain asset references and request defaults

approvals.approved_version: Exact equipment work request, directions and maintenance recipients; changes require checking again before communication.
Exact equipment specification, quantity, request version and purchasing destination; changed requisitions require checking again before submission.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=89, gross 11 minus 2 upkeep gives central net 9. Conservative case: weak asset metadata retain 9/10 lookup hours, bespoke work details retain 19/20 request hours and incompatible procurement fields retain all 10 requisition hours plus 60 fixed: 98 retained, 2 gross minus 2 =0. Compatible asset links retain 9 lookup, 15 request and 9 requisition hours plus 60 fixed: 93 retained, 7 gross minus 2 =5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain fire prevention records and logbooks

steps.what: Collect and reconcile the source information for records and logbooks
Enter factual records and logbook entries using existing linked fields
Check record completeness and correct unsupported or inconsistent entries
Save the checked entries in the existing record system

tasks.design: Use native {OPS_SYSTEM} incident-linked record fields and a source view for entries currently copied into logbooks. The specialist adds actual observations and checks completeness; ordinary same-system saves remain fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing incident facts can be copied repeatedly into separate logbook fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native incident references and reusable fields can reduce repeated transcription without generating new observations.
tasks.still_hard: Source records can omit the observations needed for an accurate account.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a recorded fact from an unsupported assumption.
tasks.altitude: Maintain one traceable factual account with less repeated typing.

reach.learn: Reuse source facts while keeping observed details explicit.

evidence.claim: NIPV incident dashboards use control-room incident figures; this establishes existing structured incident information, not a measured logbook-entry saving.

assumptions: The statement explicitly requires records and logbooks. Task-specific work requests or regulatory notices are counted once if the same entry also appears in adjacent tasks.

Control-room staff produce incident identifiers, times, locations and units in existing dispatch work; field personnel produce their observations during current operations. S1 includes retrieval and reconciliation, and retained s2 time includes capturing missing factual observations. Missing source values remain manual entry, never invented prefill.

The source view removes 5 navigation hours. Linked fields remove 24.75 hours of repeated incident headings and factual transcription from the 45-hour entry step; original observations and corrections remain retained.
Try native incident-linked fields first. No automatic alert, record import or external report is implied. S4 retains all existing save time without an author approval stage.
unknowns: How much current entry repeats already structured incident information.
Whether current records already share incident fields.
research_questions: Replay several logbook entries and measure repeated typing separately from original observation capture and correction.

already_counted.description: Check and correct the logbook account

incremental.description: Maintain linked record fields and source references

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=70.25, gross 29.75 minus 2 upkeep gives central net 27.75. Conservative case: incomplete source metadata retain 24/25 source hours and mostly original observations retain 41/45 entry hours plus 30 fixed: 95 retained, 5 gross minus 2 =3. Compatible incident-linked fields retain 22 source and 27 entry hours plus 30 fixed: 79 retained, 21 gross minus 2 =19.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Administer forest sanitation, prevention and correction regulations

steps.what: Retrieve current regulations and relevant case history
Inspect circumstances relevant to sanitation, fire prevention or violation corrections
Capture the case facts used to support the regulatory decision
Determine the applicable regulatory response and required corrections
Write the case-specific regulatory notice or correction instructions
Deliver the checked regulatory notice to the affected party

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} views for current regulations and notice headings, keeping inspection facts in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} case record. The specialist retains regulatory judgement and individual notice wording, then checks the exact notice and recipient before delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating current references and repeating notice headings adds clerical work to case administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled references and authorised notice formats support limited navigation and formatting reductions.
tasks.still_hard: The appropriate regulatory response depends on evidence and circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: Exercise proportionate judgement and explain required corrections.
tasks.altitude: Support traceable regulatory administration without automatic enforcement decisions.

reach.learn: Link the actual finding to the applicable current requirement.

evidence.claim: Native controlled-reference views and notice headings could reduce limited clerical work; regulatory decisions and savings remain unmeasured.

assumptions: This scenario includes the current evidence record supporting the decision and the notice read by the affected party. No trailing activity log is added; record work overlapping task 11108 is counted once.

Document owners maintain current regulation versions. The specialist observes facts in s2 and captures location, date and factual findings in s3, fully retaining that time. Existing case details identify the affected party; missing facts require investigation before a notice is prepared.
The reference view removes 3 navigation hours. Notice headings remove only 2 hours of repeated case identifiers and formatting, retaining individual regulatory reasoning.
No automatic enforcement, correction alert or send is proposed. Ordinary internal saves remain fully retained without self-approval.
unknowns: Whether notice formats are already configured.
How much reference navigation occurs today.
research_questions: Observe current cases and time lookup and notice formatting separately from inspection and regulatory judgement.

already_counted.description: Capture case evidence and determine the regulatory response

incremental.description: Maintain controlled references and notice headings

approvals.approved_version: Exact notice, case findings, required corrections and affected-party recipient; changed wording or recipients require a fresh check before delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=95, gross 5 minus 1 upkeep gives central net 4. Conservative case: poorly indexed regulations retain all 15 lookup hours and a bespoke notice retains 19/20 writing hours plus 65 fixed: 99 retained, 1 gross minus 1 =0. Compatible references and notice headings retain 13 lookup and 19 writing hours plus 65 fixed: 97 retained, 3 gross minus 1 =2.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain prevention, maintenance and regulatory judgement while reducing specific repeated preparation and record entry.
reach: Coordinate source facts with maintenance, control-room and case-record owners.
role.ambitious_version: Prevention specialists supported by useful current records and materials without automatic safety or enforcement decisions.
